Amazon’s algorithm recommended a Disney World guidebook to me recently. It was so incredibly bad – so obviously written by AI – that I spent a night looking at other, equally horrible examples. I thought y’all would enjoy seeing them.

Besides the fact that these books are often obviously incorrect, the larger issue is that they’re flooding the book market. It looks like Amazon lists from 10 to 20 AI-generated guidebooks for every one book that’s written by human authors. So just finding a book written by a person is a “needle in a haystack” problem and it’s getting worse. Some of these Amazon books contained obviously faked 5-star reviews as well, so relying on ratings alone won’t solve the problem.

A couple of things before we get started: I’m 99% sure that these are AI-generated books. I could be wrong – some of it could just be really, really bad human writers with a tenuous grasp on English. And reality. Here are some of the signs I look for when deciding if something is likely written by AI:

- Self-published

- Between 140 and 220 pages

- Author has no online presence except book titles

- Common AI tics like “you think it’s this , but it’s that “, overuse of words like “honest” and “genuine”, and so on

- Images of the parks that aren’t physically possible

- Images that still have the AI watermarks

- Obviously incorrect maps

- Obviously outdated information, like recommending Splash Mountain in 2027, that no human editor would let into print

With those disclaimers, let’s get started.

#### Walt Disney World Travel Guide 2027: Castles, Coasters, and Honest Planning for FirstTime and Returning Families

“Honest”. LOL. Also, “FirstTime” is one word in the book title. My editor would be incandescent with rage .

Here’s an image of Walt Disney World from the book:

There’s so much wrong here it’s hard to know where to start. In the lower left, did you know that the monorail has a 4-way intersection? I didn’t. I also didn’t know EPCOT was just behind Storybook Circus in the Magic Kingdom. Well that’s convenient anyway. I mean, we’ve apparently lost Big Thunder Mountain, Tiana’s Bayou Adventure, and the rest of Frontierland. But that’s a small price to pay for having the parks so walkable.

The “Comprehensive Detailed Map” of the resort is even better:

It’s hard to read (blurry text is another hallmark of AI-generated images). But there’s so much wrong here:

- One EPCOT – there are two on the map! – now sits on top of the Polynesian Resort – bonus points for walkability?

- There’s a walkway from the Magic Kingdom to a second EPCOT that continues on to Blizzard Beach and Typhoon Lagoon

- There are two Blizzard Beaches

- The locations of Bay Lake and Seven Seas Lagoon are switched

- The two “EPCOT Resort Area” markers (9) span the entire east-west run of Disney property

#### Unofficial Family Guide to Disneyland with Kids: Family Guide to Rides, Food, Lightning Lane Strategies & Meltdown-Free Itineraries

Bonus points for using the words “Unofficial” and “Guide” in the title. Let’s start with the book’s cover image:

Obviously, that’s not what Disneyland looks like. There’s no carousel on Main Street USA, for one thing. Also, what’s with the army of blue shirt-wearing clones forming a line around the central hub? When did rope drop become Squid Games?

The book’s highlights, though, are its maps:

Once again, there’s so much wrong that it’s hard to pick a start. I, for one, did not realize there’s a lake in front of Main Street USA. I guess that’s why Disneyland is on Harbor Boulevard? Or that Disney moved Tomorrowland to make way for Star Wars: Galaxy’s Edge. I’m not sure if Disneyland sits on the San Andreas Fault, but clearly plate tectonics have moved New Orleans Square in between Adventureland and Main Street USA.

The book gets bonus points for having a second map of Disneyland that puts the lands in completely different places than the first:

Mickey’s Toontown is in approximately the right place, but its newest attraction, Runaway Railway, has replaced all of Tomorrowland and parts of Fantasyland. Maybe those rumors about demolishing the Matterhorn are true. Finally, I don’t know what Disneyland’s “Meltdown Management Zone” is, but I hope it offers Lightning Lane.

#### Disneyland Paris Travel Guide 2026: Explore More, Wait Less & Experience the Magic

Whoever published this book left the “generated by MetaAI” watermarks in the images:

Again, no human editor would let this into print, even if the author wanted to.

Let’s pop over to Orlando for the next guide book.

#### Walt Disney World Travel Guide 2026–2027: Your Ultimate Guide to Magical Adventures, Hidden Gems, and Stress-Free Planning in the Most Magical Place on Earth

Another one with AI-generated images. Take a look of this, which I think is supposed to be the Magic Kingdom’s Central Hub at night. It comes off as post-zombie apocalypse meets Alice in Wonderland cosplay:

I cannot imagine the conversation I’d need to have with a publisher in order to get that photo into print.

#### Walt Disney World Travel Guide 2026–2027: The Practical A-to-Z Planning Guide for First-Timers, Families, Budget Travelers, and Returning Fans

I love the Walt Disney World map in this one:

Hey kids – I’ve parked the car by the side of the road. Let’s all run into the spooky woods!

On to the last book of the day.

#### The Ultimate Disney World Playbook: An Unofficial Blueprint for Stress-Free Magic: Your Complete Insider Guide to Lightning Lanes, Budgeting, Accessibility, Dining & Every Park — Done Right

More AI-generated images. Here’s one with a background of Cinderella Castle and … a car parking lot?

And here’s one of some generic park entrance – it’s not Disney World. There’s a physical turnstile, which Disney no longer has, but no matter. And yes, the turnstile is in the middle of an open walkway, which kinda defeats the purpose of a turnstile. Ignore that too. A close look at the turnstile shows it has a giant metal bar completely blocking entry.

As I said before, Amazon is flooded with these AI-generated books. There’s tons more to marvel at. In the comments below, let me know if you find one that’s especially bad. We may include it in a next round of reviews.
